output.methodChoice: Compared job-level printer records (X10) with the ERP shelf-life audit trail (X9) to test each hypothesis against the timing and the operator overrides.
output.brief: The wrong expiry dates were not caused by operators, the firmware upgrade or the agency staff. Printer job records show the correct 24-month value on every job up to 3 Oct. From 4 Oct, PackBridge sent a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol, and the printer printed exactly what it received. No operator overrides were recorded on any of the 47 jobs. The ERP audit trail shows the 36-month value was entered on 3 Oct with a valid-from date of March 2027, yet it was used in October. That points to the data interface, not people, which contradicts the vendor's claim that future values cannot reach the line. Confidence is moderate: the mechanism of how the future value was released is not yet confirmed. Next steps: hold all Veltranol lots packed since 4 Oct, not just the three, and restore the 24-month value. Check the interface configuration, and add a second-person check of expiry against the batch record. Do not remove or warn the agency operators, and do not switch off the camera. Check other products changed in October, including HX-15-30 and MR-05-14, before drawing conclusions about them.
